salient_findings: Coagulative necrosis with frequent karyorrhexis and a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate on biopsy
key_facts: 45-year-old man
Three-week history of axillary lump
One week history of low-grade fever
Tender, non-mobile, 3 × 4 cm lymph node in the left axilla
History of hypertension
History of laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass
Smoker, 30 cigarettes daily
Takes vitamin and mineral supplements

Normal or negative laboratory studies, including complete blood count, ESR, liver and renal panels, autoantibodies, complement levels, inflammatory markers, thyroid function, and serologies for viral and parasitic pathogens
Unremarkable thoracoabdominal CT scan except for axillary lymphadenopathy
Biopsy of axillary node revealed coagulative necrosis with frequent karyorrhexis and a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate
Investigation for mycobacteria was negative

shortlist.label: Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological findings of coagulative necrosis with frequent karyorrhexis and a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate are consistent with this disease

shortlist.label: Cat-scratch disease
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute axillary lymphadenopathy with fever is a common presentation of this disease

shortlist.label: Histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical and histopathological features are similar to those of this disease

shortlist.label: Tuberculous lymphadenitis
shortlist.why_kept: Although the investigation for mycobacteria was negative, this disease remains a possibility due to its high prevalence and the patient's history of smoking

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of a tender, non-mobile lymph node and systemic symptoms such as fever warrant consideration of this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a tender, slow-growing axillary lump, low-grade fever, and a biopsy showing coagulative necrosis with frequent karyorrhexis and a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate is consistent with Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease, a rare form of histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis.

rejected.label: Cat-scratch disease
rejected.why: No mention of cat exposure or scratch history

rejected.label: Histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis
rejected.why: This is another term for Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease, making it redundant

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Biopsy results and clinical presentation do not support lymphoma
